verdict_reason: All 4 hard gates pass, but average 6.9 < 8 and four items (stakes, escalation, surprise = 6) are below 7. Solid, clean, correct premise; not yet hookable enough and the middle is narrated storybook rather than a twist-driven story.

checks.math: Recomputed with .venv/Scripts/python: 2013-09-17 to 2026-11-19 = 4,811 days; x $0.02 = $96.22; minus $79.99 = $16.23; 1 cent/day = $48.11. All correct. Spoken 'ninety-six' and 'sixteen' are safe round-downs. Note: $79.99 is pre-tax; with sales tax (~$85) the jar still covers it, so the claim holds, but 'kept sixteen dollars' is then slightly generous (about $11 after typical tax). Say 'kept over ten dollars' only if you want to be strict; acceptable as is.
checks.word_count: Spoken (say) words counted = 74, not 71. Inside 55-75 but ONE word from the cap; every fix must be word-neutral. Real am_liam @0.9 speed is slower than the 2.3 w/s estimate would imply only if padded: expect about 26-31 s with pauses, lower half of the window.
checks.scenes: 10 scenes, within 8-12. On-screen text all <= 5 words. No ph/Taglish anywhere.
checks.extra_1_hook_completeness: Does not mislead (the span arrives in line 2 and 4, and the whole video is that claim). But as heard alone, 'two cents a day, you could buy GTA 6' is literally incomplete and invites 'that is impossible' (curiosity gap, fine) and then deflates when the answer is 'thirteen years': a 1 a.m. viewer thinks 'of course, 13 years of anything buys $80'. Withholding the span is a legitimate gap, but the reveal of the span (line 2) is a throwaway clause, not a beat. Either keep the gap and make 'thirteen years' land as a deliberate beat, or test 'since 2013' in the hook (your own title already uses it). Mild weakening, not a fail.
checks.extra_2_hype: Partly rides it. 'GTA 6' is in the first 2 s (good for search and hype). But the video never says the game is out NOW/this week and never uses the real hype hook the research found (13 years since GTA 5, 'GTA flu'). Line 5 'Game day came' is past tense: if posted Nov 17-18 (as the research notes advise) it is wrong, because the game is not out yet; and 'Game day' does not say which game. 'GTA 6' is spoken once only, in the first line; the payoff never re-names it.
checks.extra_3_ip: Clean. 'GTA 6' only as plain-text topic and spoken; generic blank box, no logo/art/footage/music/characters; plain cartoon city; 'NOT FINANCIAL ADVICE' badge plus description note. Watch only: do not show 'GTA 6' in Rockstar's lettering/colors in scene 1 (plain white outlined headline is fine). 'Tiny habits beat panic' is not a guaranteed-outcome claim.
checks.drawability: Mostly feasible with docs/scene-format.md. Problems: scene 5 'Crowd panic gag' has no crowd character (only benny + cast; use one stranger plus cash prop flying, or drop it). Scene 4 calendar counter 2013->2026 via counter item may render '2,013' with a thousands separator; check or use a headline/badge swap. Scene 6 packs stamp + counter + coins + stranger reaction + flash in a short line (8 words); keep to stamp, counter, coins. Scene 10 split screen is two characters plus a list: feasible but crowded.

fixes: Line 1 (hook, 7): the span is hidden, so 'two cents a day' sounds small and impossible with no picture of time. Either test 'If you saved two cents a day since 2013, you could buy G T A six.' (and shorten line 2 to 'Benny started a coin jar that year.' to stay word-neutral), or keep the gap but make line 2 a punchy beat: 'Benny tried it. It took thirteen years.' Keep total spoken words <= 75.

Line 2 (stakes, 6): the viewer is 'you' in line 1, then Benny takes over for the rest ('Benny started... Benny saved... Benny smashed...'). Earlier QA found switching from 'you' to third person weakens stakes. Make it the viewer's story or tie Benny to the viewer: e.g. line 2 'Benny did exactly that, in twenty thirteen.' and line 7 ending 'You could do it too.'; the final A/B question already returns to 'you', keep that.

Line 3 (escalation, 6): 'His friend laughed at him' never says WHY (audio-only viewers get no reason; the 'TOO SMALL!' text carries it). Change to 'His friend said two cents is too small.' and cut line 8 or line 4 words to stay at 75.

Lines 2 and 4 (escalation, 6): both say 'Benny started/saved coins for years'; the same information twice. Merge: line 4 -> 'He kept going for thirteen years.' (also makes the 13-year span the deliberate beat) and spend the saved words on line 5.

Line 5 (surprise, 6; clarity, 7; facts, 8): 'Game day came, and everyone was broke.' is a non-sequitur: why is everyone broke, and what game? 'broke' is slang for a non-native listener, 'everyone' is unsupported hyperbole (it is one friend), and 'came' is wrong tense before Nov 19. Replace with two plain sentences: 'Then G T A six came out. His friend had no money.' (and fix the visual: no crowd, only the stranger). This also re-names the game, ties to the hype and makes the friend's fate the twist.

Line 8 (ending, 7; entertainment, 7): 'Tiny habits beat panic.' is a lecture-style moral (owner rejected lecture videos), and 'panic' does not match what happened (the friend was broke, not panicking). Cut it and use the freed 4 words on lines 3 and 5. Let the story say it with the confetti beat on line 7.
Line 9 (ending, 7): 'panic later' is vague and loaded. Use a plain A/B: 'Would you save daily, or spend it all?' and on-screen 'A: SAVE  B: SPEND'.

Line 6-7 (payoff, 7): the payoff is correct but modest ($96 over 13 years). Add a visible gag so it feels earned: the jar of pennies is heavy and Benny can barely lift it, or the cashier counts coins one by one (research suggested a tiny abacus). The 'sixteen dollars left' is a nice cherry; keep.
Timing note: post on or after Nov 19 (or change line 5 to future/present tense) so 'came out' is true. Posting Nov 17-18 as the research note suggests contradicts the past-tense script.
